req.title: Deleting all tasks leaves empty table
req.statement: The system shall leave GET /tasks/ returning [] after every task has been deleted.
triggers: deleting all tasks leaves empty table

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that after all tasks are deleted, a GET request to /tasks/ should return an empty list. This behavior needs to be verified through positive, negative, and boundary test cases to ensure robustness against common mutations.

tests.name: test_delete_all_tasks_positive
preconditions: At least one task exists in the system.
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Create a task to ensure there is at least one task
response = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Test Task", "description": "Test Description", "completed": False})
assert response.status_code == 201
created_task_id = response.json()["id"]

# Delete the created task
response = client.delete(f"/tasks/{created_task_id}")
assert response.status_code == 204

# Verify that GET /tasks/ returns an empty list
response = client.get("/tasks/")
assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.json() == []

tests.name: test_delete_nonexistent_task_negative
preconditions: No task exists with the given ID.
actions: Attempt to delete a task with a non-existent ID using DELETE /tasks/{id}.
expected: HTTP 404 Not Found error is returned.
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Attempt to delete a task with a non-existent ID
non_existent_id = 9999
response = client.delete(f"/tasks/{non_existent_id}")
assert response.status_code == 404
assert response.json()["detail"] == f"Task with id {non_existent_id} not found"

tests.name: test_delete_all_tasks_boundary
preconditions: Exactly one task exists in the system.
actions: Delete the only existing task using DELETE /tasks/{id}.
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Create exactly one task
response = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Boundary Task", "description": "Boundary Description", "completed": False})
assert response.status_code == 201
created_task_id = response.json()["id"]

# Delete the only existing task
response = client.delete(f"/tasks/{created_task_id}")
assert response.status_code == 204

# Verify that GET /tasks/ returns an empty list
response = client.get("/tasks/")
assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.json() == []
